database.name: Chinook
database.description: The catalog and sales database of a digital music store (the MelodyStream BI scenario). It models a music catalog (artists, albums, tracks, genres, media types), people (customers and employees/support reps), sales (invoices and their line items), and curated playlists. It answers questions about what sells, who buys, which staff support which customers, and how the catalog is organized.

Artist.description: A recording artist or band. One row per artist.

ArtistId.description: Surrogate primary key for the artist.

Name.notes: Nullable in schema but populated in practice.

Album.description: An album released by an artist. One row per album.

AlbumId.description: Surrogate primary key for the album.

sample_values: For Those About To Rock We Salute You

ArtistId.description: The artist who released this album.

Track.description: A single track/song in the catalog. Central table joining catalog (album/genre/media type) to sales (invoice lines) and playlists. One row per track.

TrackId.description: Surrogate primary key for the track.

sample_values: For Those About To Rock (We Salute You)

AlbumId.description: The album this track belongs to.
AlbumId.notes: Nullable — some tracks have no album.

MediaTypeId.description: The media/file type of this track.

GenreId.notes: Nullable — some tracks have no genre.

sample_values: Angus Young, Malcolm Young, Brian Johnson

Milliseconds.notes: Divide by 1000 for seconds, by 60000 for minutes.

Bytes.description: File size of the track in bytes.

UnitPrice.description: Catalog list price of the track (per unit).
UnitPrice.notes: The sale price actually charged is on InvoiceLine.UnitPrice.

Genre.description: A music genre used to classify tracks. One row per genre.

GenreId.description: Surrogate primary key for the genre.

MediaType.description: The media/file format a track is stored in. One row per media type.

MediaTypeId.description: Surrogate primary key for the media type.

Playlist.description: A curated playlist. Tracks are attached via the PlaylistTrack junction table. One row per playlist. NOTE: several playlists share the same Name (e.g. two 'Music' playlists) — duplicate names are real and expected.

PlaylistId.description: Surrogate primary key for the playlist.

Name.notes: Duplicate names exist; group by PlaylistId (and Name) to keep them distinct.

PlaylistTrack.description: Junction table mapping playlists to tracks (many-to-many). One row per (playlist, track) membership.
PlaylistTrack.grain: one track's membership in one playlist

Customer.description: A customer of the store. Each customer is optionally assigned a support rep (an employee). One row per customer.

CustomerId.description: Surrogate primary key for the customer.

sample_values: Embraer - Empresa Brasileira de Aeronáutica S.A.

SupportRepId.description: The employee (support rep) assigned to this customer.

Employee.description: An employee of the store. Employees can be support reps for customers and report to other employees (self-referencing hierarchy via ReportsTo). One row per employee.

EmployeeId.description: Surrogate primary key for the employee.

ReportsTo.description: The employee this person reports to (manager).
ReportsTo.notes: Self-referencing; null for the top manager.

HireDate.notes: Filter/group by year with strftime('%Y', HireDate).

Invoice.description: A sales invoice issued to a customer on a date, with a billing address and a grand total. One row per invoice. Use Invoice.Total for whole-invoice / per-customer / per-country revenue; use InvoiceLine for per-track/genre/album revenue.

InvoiceId.description: Surrogate primary key for the invoice.

CustomerId.description: The customer billed on this invoice.

InvoiceDate.notes: Filter/group by period with strftime, e.g. strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2021'. Data spans 2021-2025.

BillingCountry.description: Billing country. Convenient for per-country revenue without joining Customer.

Total.description: Grand total charged on the invoice (sum of its line items).
Total.notes: Use for whole-invoice / per-customer / per-country revenue. For per-track/genre/album/media-type revenue, sum InvoiceLine.UnitPrice*Quantity instead.

InvoiceLine.description: A single line item on an invoice: which track was bought, at what unit price, and quantity. The grain for detailed sales analysis (revenue by track/genre/album/media type). One row per line item.
InvoiceLine.grain: one line item on one invoice

InvoiceLineId.description: Surrogate primary key for the line item.

InvoiceId.description: The invoice this line belongs to.

TrackId.description: The track sold on this line.

UnitPrice.description: Price charged per unit on this line.
UnitPrice.notes: Revenue for a line = UnitPrice * Quantity.

Quantity.description: Number of units sold on this line.

relationships.description: Each album belongs to one artist.
Each track belongs to at most one album.
Each track has at most one genre.
Each track has one media/file type.
Each sold line item references the track sold.
Each line item belongs to one invoice.
Each invoice belongs to one customer.
Each customer may be assigned a support-rep employee.

common_metrics.name: total sales / revenue (detailed)
common_metrics.definition: Revenue at the line-item grain, for breakdowns by track, genre, album, media type, or artist.
common_metrics.notes: This is the correct revenue for per-track/genre/album/media-type/artist questions. Do NOT use Invoice.Total for these.

common_metrics.name: total revenue (whole invoice / customer / country)
common_metrics.definition: Revenue aggregated at the invoice level.
common_metrics.notes: Use for overall revenue, revenue per customer, or revenue per (billing) country/period.

common_metrics.name: average invoice total
common_metrics.notes: Group by BillingCountry for per-country averages.

common_metrics.name: number of customers
common_metrics.definition: Count of customers, optionally per country or per support rep.
common_metrics.notes: Per support rep: COUNT(Customer.CustomerId) grouped by Employee via Customer.SupportRepId.

common_metrics.name: tracks per group (count)
common_metrics.definition: Number of tracks per playlist / genre / media type / album.
common_metrics.notes: For playlists use LEFT JOIN PlaylistTrack so empty playlists count 0; group by PlaylistId and Name.

common_metrics.name: revenue by time period
common_metrics.definition: Revenue grouped/filtered by year or month.

join_paths.description: Revenue or units sold by genre (best-selling genres).
Count tracks per media type (most popular format).

join_paths.path: Artist.ArtistId = Album.ArtistId AND Album.AlbumId = Track.AlbumId AND Track.TrackId = InvoiceLine.TrackId
join_paths.description: Revenue or units sold by artist.
Customers assigned to each support rep (employee with most customers).
Revenue or invoice counts per customer.
Tracks in each playlist; use LEFT JOIN to include empty playlists.

dialect_notes: SQLite dialect. Date filtering/grouping uses strftime, e.g. strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2021' or strftime('%Y-%m', InvoiceDate).
String concatenation uses || , e.g. FirstName || ' ' || LastName AS Name.
Identifiers are case-sensitive as written (Genre, InvoiceLine, SupportRepId).
Several playlists share the same Name; group by PlaylistId (and Name) and expect duplicate-named rows — this is correct, do not add DISTINCT to hide it.
Monetary columns (UnitPrice, Total) are NUMERIC(10,2); round to 2 decimals when presenting.
Only read-only SELECT/CTE queries are permitted; no writes, DDL, PRAGMA, or multiple statements.
